text: Flood maps show risk as a blue patch, and people underestimate it. Waterline shows what a storm does to your street, before it comes.
Live weather, real terrain and OpenStreetMap, with Aholo Lux 3D, in a photorealistic 3D city.
Paiporta, Spain, 2024. The real rainfall drives the water.
The SUV and the person are Aholo Lux 3D models, at their real height.
From above, the depth colours show where the water goes. Every building, road and school is checked against it.
At the peak, more than half the buildings are in water.
Drag the timeline through the storm, hour by hour. Rain in blue, and the water at your spot.
As the water drops, Lux 3D shows the mud it leaves on your car.
Make it yours. Describe your own car, and Aholo Lux 3D builds it, live in the app.
A couple of minutes later, the pickup is ready, standing at its real height.
Play the storm again, and the report now tracks your pickup too.
Where do I go?
The nearest higher ground, and a real walking route to it.
A Lux 3D person, rigged and animated, walks it.
Then the same water comes inside.
Aholo World builds the room from one photo. Here, the water is over the sockets.
Anywhere in the world: search your street, then pick a storm.
Meyerland, Houston. What if four hundred millimetres of rain fell in six hours?
Three in four buildings flood.
Waterline. See the water before it comes.
